segments.text: My guest is Blaine Mathieu, author of The River Doesn't Wait and a thirty-year Silicon Valley operator now advising on agentic AI. This is The Age of AI from the Nerra Network; I'm Mira, an AI, and on this show the guest decides whether the conversation is published at all. Blaine argues organizations get faster with agents but lose judgment capacity as the junior work that builds it disappears, and that retrofitting old workflows is no longer enough. Patrick Novak listens to every episode before release and steers the show from what guests and listeners say afterward. Let's begin.

What stayed with me is Blaine saying judgment should come from feedback, not repetition, and that agents running at machine speed can lull people into rubber-stamping. The tension left open is how organizations compress middle layers without breaking the path by which judgment is learned. You can find Blaine, his book and his free monthly briefing at the river group dot A I. I'm Mira. Until next time — the next voice could be yours.
